facts.detail: Ofcom published the Nations report 2025 on 19 November 2025.
The page summarises broadband and mobile availability for each UK nation.
Full fibre was available to 79% of residential premises in England, up 10 percentage points.
Gigabit-capable coverage reached 88%, or 21.1 million premises, in England.
Where full fibre was available in England, take-up reached 41%, up eight percentage points.
Satellite broadband connections in England increased from around 70,000 to 90,000.
Around 26,000 English premises could not access decent fixed-line or FWA broadband, 7,000 fewer than a year earlier.
England 5G standalone coverage outside premises was 85% at High Confidence and 75% at Very High Confidence.
At least one MNO provided 5G coverage to 81% of England's landmass, up from 76%.
All four MNOs provided 4G coverage to 90% of England's landmass.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2025 update on 8 May 2025.
The report provides a snapshot as of January 2025.
It is an interim update to Connected Nations 2024.
Ofcom notes considerable uncertainty when assessing mobile coverage at a particular low-signal location.
Fixed broadband reporting covers fixed-line and FWA networks.
Gigabit-capable broadband reached 25.9 million homes, or 86%.
Full fibre reached 22.5 million homes, or 74%.
Full-fibre connections increased by 1.5 million to 9.0 million.
Premises without decent fixed-line or FWA broadband fell from 58,000 to 48,000.
At least one MNO was predicted to provide good outdoor 4G to 96% of UK landmass and 5G to around 62%.
